company: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc.

rfm_tuples.R: FY2023 10-K (Item 7 / MD&A): 'In 2023, we paid regular dividends of $5.20 per share and declared a dividend of $1.30 per share that was subsequently paid on August 8, 2023 ... totaling $144,302 dividends declared or paid in 2023, and repurchasing $17,449 in shares of our common stock.' + Cash flow statement: dividends $114,302; FY23 net cash from ops $250,457; capex $124,319; net income $99,050.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B - Derive: payout ratio = $144M dividends / $99M net income = 145% in FY23. FCF after capex = $250M - $124M = $126M; dividends alone consumed 91% of post-capex cash. The 10-K's framing ('focus on generating shareholder returns') implies sustainability; arithmetic implies the dividend is uncovered by net income and barely covered by FCF in the strongest year of the cycle.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY23 dividends paid (cash) $114.3M; FY23 net income $99.05M; dividend coverage 0.87x by net income, 1.10x by FCF (op cash $250.5M - capex $124.3M = $126.1M / $114.3M). FY23 op income $120.6M was -21% YoY (vs $153.0M FY22) and 67% below FY21 normalized $366.7M. Comp traffic -3.5% in FY23 (per MD&A), masked by 8.6% menu price take. Q1 FY24 net income $5.5M (-68% YoY) and Q2 FY24 net income $26.5M (-13% YoY) per pre-cutoff 10-Qs (Nov 2023, Feb 2024). Dividend was nonetheless maintained at $1.30/qtr through Q2 FY24 = $58.5M paid against $32.0M six-month net income.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Dividend was paying out >100% of trailing earnings before the cutoff and ~180% of six-month FY24 earnings. The 10-K's 'subject to compliance with all laws and agreements' boilerplate (Risk Factors) admits no guarantee but the 'returning capital to shareholders' framing in MD&A omits any FCF reconciliation. Mode-B inference: a dividend cut is mathematically implied by trajectory (traffic -4.0%/-5.5% Q2/H1 FY24, op income -33% H1 FY24, revolver drawn $156.5M vs $120M at YE) - the dividend is the next capital-allocation domino.

rfm_tuples.R: FY2023 10-K Item 1A Risk Factor: 'Given the significant uncertainty relating to the macroeconomic environment, there are potential scenarios under which we could fail to comply with these covenants, which would result in an event of default that, if not waived, could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations or ability to continue to service our debt obligations.' + 'we cannot provide any guarantee of future cash dividend payments or that we will be able to actively repurchase our common stock pursuant to a share repurchase program.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Verify covenant terms in credit agreement description and current compliance status; Mode B - derive that explicit risk-factor language naming covenant breach as 'potential scenario' is rare for a non-distressed restaurant operator and implies management modeled the breach.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1A risk factor + Q2 FY24 10-Q (filed 2024-02-27) Note 4 Debt
rfm_tuples.M_value: 2022 Revolving Credit Facility ($700M, expires Jun 2027) carries 'maximum consolidated total senior secured leverage ratio and minimum consolidated interest coverage ratio'. As of Jul 28, 2023: $120M drawn, $32.5M LCs. As of Jan 26, 2024: $156.5M drawn (+30% in 6 months). Weighted avg rate 6.96% (Jan 26, 2024) - rising from prior period. Company states it is 'in compliance' at both dates but provides no headroom metric. $300M 0.625% Convertible Notes due Jun 2026 require refinancing in ~25 months. Risk factor explicitly contemplates failure-to-comply scenarios - distressed-issuer-style language that did not appear in pre-pandemic 10-Ks of this issuer (claim evolution).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Currently compliant but management has chosen to install explicit covenant-breach language in Item 1A, which is unusual for a steady cash-flowing restaurant. Convertible Notes due 2026 must be refinanced into a much-higher-rate environment (current revolver 6.96% vs 0.625% on Notes - a 600+ bps step-up if refinanced as straight debt) - an order-of-magnitude jump in interest expense relative to the $17M FY23 interest line. Revolver utilization rose from 17% to 22% of capacity in 6 months while operating income fell. The risk factor's plain reading - a near-term covenant problem is possible - is the Mode-B signal.

rfm_tuples.R: Q1 FY2024 10-Q (filed 2023-11-30, period ended 2023-10-27): Q1 revenue $823.8M (-1.9% YoY), op income $11.4M (-52% YoY), net income $5.5M (-68% YoY); '$1.30 per share' dividend maintained. Q2 FY2024 10-Q (filed 2024-02-27): Q2 revenue flat $935.4M, op income $30.8M (-21% YoY), six-month op income $42.2M (-33% YoY). Q2 MD&A: 'we continued to make progress on the strategic transformation initiative that began during the first quarter of 2024' and Q2 incremental cost includes 'Chief Executive Officer transition costs incurred in 2024' and 'severance costs related to corporate restructuring.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Verify quarterly trajectory and CEO transition timing against EDGAR filings; Mode B - derive that 'strategic transformation initiative' announced concurrent with CEO change + restructuring severance is the operational-distress signature.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Quarterly net income trajectory: Q4'22=$28.6M (impl) -> Q1'23=$17.1M -> Q1'24=$5.5M (-68%) -> Q2'24=$26.5M (-13%). H1 FY24 op income $42.2M annualizes to ~$84M vs FY23 $120M (-30%) and FY21 normalized $366M (-77%). CEO Sandra Cochran (in role since 2011) departure language present in CEO-transition-cost disclosure in Q2 FY24. Strategic-transformation initiative explicitly NOT disclosed in the Sept 2023 10-K - first appeared in Q1 FY24 10-Q (Nov 2023). Restructuring severance booked in H1 FY24. Comp guest traffic Q2 FY24 = -4.0%, H1 FY24 = -5.5% per 10-Q table (already worse than FY23's -3.5%).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Claim evolution between the FY23 10-K (Sept 2023) and the Q1+Q2 FY24 10-Qs is materially negative: a CEO transition, a corporate-restructuring/severance program, and a 'strategic transformation initiative' all appeared within four months of the 10-K filing. The 10-K's stated FY24 outlook ('continuing our continued focus on generating shareholder returns ... we believe ... will be sufficient for the next twelve months') contains no advance disclosure of the transformation program or CEO succession. Operational deterioration (traffic from -3.5% FY23 to -5.5% H1 FY24) is real-time worsening, not a one-quarter blip.

rfm_tuples.R: FY2023 10-K Item 1 Business: 'The average check per guest during 2023 was $13.36, which represents a 10.3% increase over the prior year.' + MD&A: 'Our comparable store restaurant sales increase in 2023 ... resulted from an average check increase of 9.8% (including an 8.6% average menu price increase) partially offset by a decrease in guest traffic of 3.5%.' + 'Off-premise sales represented approximately 20% of restaurant sales volumes in both 2023 and 2022.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B - Derive: a 10.3% check increase composed of 8.6 ppt menu price + 1.2 ppt mix means real customer behavior worsened (-3.5% traffic) and FY23's headline comp gain is entirely a price-take phenomenon. At a moderately-priced family restaurant with a 56-year-old core demographic, repeated price hikes are demand-destructive.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1 + MD&A Key Performance Indicators + Q2 FY24 10-Q
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY23 menu price action: +8.6%. Q2 FY24 menu price action: +4.8%. Trailing-six-quarter cumulative menu price action approximately +14-15%. FY23 traffic: -3.5%. H1 FY24 traffic: -5.5% (accelerating decline). Average check FY23 = $13.36; this is moderate-price family-dining segment where competitive substitutes (IHOP, Denny's, fast-casual) compete on value. 10-K explicitly says off-premise = 20% of restaurant sales, unchanged YoY, suggesting the post-pandemic delivery growth lever has tapped out. Q2 FY24 MD&A attributes traffic decreases to 'macroeconomic factors, including inflationary pressures, higher interest rates, higher consumer debt levels, lower savings rates and the risk of recession' - blaming exogenous demand rather than acknowledging brand/value-proposition issues.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The headline comp-sales-positive narrative is sustained only by price take; the underlying traffic curve is steepening (-3.5% -> -5.5%). The 10-K's framing 'check increase of 9.8% partially offset by traffic decrease of 3.5%' technically discloses the offset but the Item 1 'highlights' emphasize the check growth. The deeper concern: a moderate-price brand with declining traffic + late-2022 8.6% menu hike is at risk of brand-equity erosion; further price take to defend margin (the obvious management response) accelerates the traffic curve. Mode-B inference: management has limited remaining pricing power and the 'strategic transformation' is in part an attempt to find a non-price growth lever.

rfm_tuples.R: FY2023 10-K Auditor section: '/s/ Deloitte & Touche LLP Nashville, Tennessee September 26, 2023 We have served as the Company's auditor since 1974.' + 'we have concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of July 28, 2023' + ICFR attestation: 'Deloitte & Touche LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, has issued an attestation report on our internal control over financial reporting'.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Verify auditor identity, tenure, and ICFR opinion text; Mode B - derive whether auditor history is consistent with a non-distressed control environment.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Auditor: Deloitte & Touche LLP (Big 4), tenure since 1974 = 49 years. Signal=CLEAN_BIG4_TENURE. Resignation language: 0 matches. Disagreement language: 0 matches. ICFR conclusion: effective. Going concern: NO_GOING_CONCERN, 0 matches in 10-K, 0 in Q1+Q2 FY24 10-Qs. This is a clean accounting/audit posture - unlike the AAP-style cluster of material weaknesses and CFO/CAO turnover.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Accounting/audit posture is genuinely clean - not a forensic-accounting story. The thesis (if any) is operational/capital-allocation deterioration, not balance-sheet/control-quality fraud. This is an important PASS that prevents the framework from over-weighting CBRL as a 'lying' name; the disclosures are mostly honest, just inadequately weighted in the MD&A framing.

rfm_tuples.R: FY2023 10-K Item 1 Business / Suppliers section: 'Chicken is the single food item within these categories that accounted for the largest share of our food purchasing expense in 2023 at approximately 5% of total food purchases ... Eggs are purchased through five vendors. We purchase our pork through six vendors, poultry through nine vendors and beef through seven vendors.' No customer concentration disclosed (CBRL is direct-to-consumer).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Verify supplier-concentration claim and confirm no significant customer concentration risk.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Supplier concentration: low (5%+ items spread across 5-9 vendors per category). Customer concentration: not applicable (B2C restaurant). No single supplier represents >10% of cost of goods. This matches the absence of customer/supplier concentration as a top-of-funnel risk factor. Largest food purchases: poultry 14%, fruits/vegetables 14%, dairy 13%, beef 11%, pork 10%.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Supplier diversification is real and material to thesis: CBRL is not exposed to single-vendor breakage risk; commodity inflation flows through indices, not relationship-specific. PASS - the supply-side narrative is honest. Mode-B: this is one fewer asymmetric tail risk to underwrite.

rfm_tuples.R: FY2023 10-K Item 1A Capital Structure Risk Factor: 'we cannot provide any guarantee of future cash dividend payments or that we will be able to actively repurchase our common stock pursuant to a share repurchase program.' + 'Subject to the limits imposed by our revolving credit facility, in September 2021, we were authorized by our Board of Directors to repurchase shares ... up to $100,000. In the fourth quarter of 2022, we were authorized ... up to a total value of $200,000 ... On June 2, 2023, our Board of Directors extended this repurchase authorization for an additional year.' Actual FY23 buybacks: $17.4M of $200M authorized (8.7% utilization).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B - Derive: low buyback utilization despite an explicit board authorization is a soft-cash-preservation signal that management does not flag. Compare buyback dollars across cycle.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A Liquidity + Cash Flow Statement + Form 4 insider activity post-July 2023 (m_sources.form4)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Buyback cadence: FY21 $35.0M, FY22 $131.5M, FY23 $17.4M (decline of 87% vs FY22). Authorization $200M remaining largely unused. Form 4 activity post-FY23 (Aug 2023 - May 2024): 30 Form 4s, ~0 discretionary insider sales (1 small disposition by Word H L Jr Mar 22; tax-withholding 'F' transactions on RSU vesting), 22+ acquisitions/grants - typical for restricted-window mechanics. Insider posture is neutral; not signaling acute distress but also not opportunistic buying into a -47.5% drawdown.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Buyback decline of 87% YoY is consistent with cash-preservation but the 10-K does not frame it that way - management instead emphasizes dividend continuity. The combination (dividend held flat at $5.20 + buyback effectively halted) is the asymmetric outcome - management is signaling 'we will protect the dividend at the expense of buybacks.' Mode-B inference: when the dividend itself becomes uncovered (as in H1 FY24, see C1), this defense priority will be revisited. Insider passive posture (neutral) provides modest counterweight against an acute-distress reading.

rfm_tuples.R: FY2023 10-K MD&A Results of Operations table: 'Operating income 3.5% 4.7% 13.0%' (as % of revenue for 2023/2022/2021); 'Net income 2.9% 4.0% 9.0%' YoY; 'Total revenue percentage increase 5.4% 15.8% 11.8%'. + Income statement: G&A expense $174.1M (FY23) vs $157.4M (FY22) vs $147.8M (FY21) = +18% over two years.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Verify margin trajectory; Mode B - derive whether the 13.0% FY21 op margin is structural or one-off (sale-leaseback gain).
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY21 op income $366.7M included a $217.7M Gain on sale and leaseback transactions per the % table ((7.7%) gain line). Adjusted FY21 op income ex-gain = ~$148.9M (4.4% margin). So real margin trajectory: 4.4% (FY21 adj) -> 4.7% (FY22) -> 3.5% (FY23) - a -120 bps decline FY22->FY23 on top of essentially flat trailing pre-gain margins. G&A grew +18% across two years on revenue growth of +22% - operating leverage is barely positive. The 13.0% FY21 figure cited in the percentage table is misleading without explicit caveat that it includes a non-recurring gain.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The MD&A percentage table juxtaposes 3.5% / 4.7% / 13.0% without prominent caveat that the 13.0% includes a real-estate gain. A casual reader gets the impression of a structural margin collapse from 13% to 3.5%; the structural reality is closer to 4.4% -> 3.5% (a real decline, but smaller). The opposite framing distortion to AAP-style underdisclosure - here, the comparison is too pessimistic at the top of the table while the narrative is too optimistic. Severity is MODERATE because the gain is disclosed and quantified elsewhere in the same 10-K.

rfm_tuples.R: FY2023 10-K Risk Factors: 'the effects of our indebtedness and associated restrictions on our financial and operating flexibility'; 'risks and uncertainties associated with inflationary conditions with respect to the price of commodities, transportation, distribution and labor'; '$300 million aggregate principal amount of 0.625% Convertible Senior Notes due 2026.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B - Derive refinancing-cliff exposure: Convertible Notes ($300M, 0.625%) mature June 2026. Convert price likely far out-of-the-money given drawdown. Refinancing into 2025-2026 will be at materially higher rates.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note on Long-Term Debt + sec_filings m-source
rfm_tuples.M_value: 0.625% Convertible Senior Notes, $300M principal, mature Jun 15, 2026 - ~25 months from cutoff. Current revolver rate 6.96% (Jan 2024 10-Q). Implied refinancing step-up: ~600 bps. Annual incremental interest if refinanced as straight debt at 6-7%: $300M * 6.5% = $19.5M, vs $1.9M current = $17.6M additional pre-tax annual expense (~17% of FY23 op income). Convert mechanics: Notes have associated hedge and warrants from 2021 issuance, which suggests management did not expect deep OTM at maturity. Pre-cutoff drawdown -47.5% from 52w high implies share price is materially below 2021 issuance reference - convertibles likely OTM and will require cash redemption or refinancing at par.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 0.625% coupon is a Covid-era artifact that will not be repeatable. The 10-K does not run a sensitivity showing FY26 pro-forma interest expense under straight-debt refinancing. Mode-B math: $17.6M incremental annual interest, against an FY23 op income of $120.6M (declining), is a ~15% structural earnings drag on top of the operating deterioration. Combined with the dividend math in C1 and covenant structure in C2, the 2026 refi is the third leg of the balance-sheet pressure case.

rfm_tuples.R: FY2023 10-K Item 1 Business: 'continued our focus on generating shareholder returns by paying $5.20 per share in dividends for fiscal 2023 and declaring a dividend of $1.30 per share' + Item 1 Strategy: 'Enhancing our business model through our cost savings program and investing in technology.' No mention of a 'strategic transformation initiative,' no mention of CEO succession planning, no mention of restructuring/severance program.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A - Claim evolution: compare 10-K (Sept 26, 2023) cost-savings/strategy language vs Q1+Q2 FY24 10-Qs (Nov 30, 2023 and Feb 27, 2024); Mode B - derive whether the 10-K's strategic posture was already obsolete on the day it was filed.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1 + Q1 FY24 10-Q (filed 2023-11-30, 65 days after 10-K) + Q2 FY24 10-Q (filed 2024-02-27)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K language (filed Sep 26, 2023): 'cost savings program' (incremental). Q1 FY24 10-Q language (filed Nov 30, 2023): 'strategic transformation initiative that began during the first quarter of 2024 ... comprehensive review of the business and a wide-ranging assessment of near-term and long-term opportunities and strategic objectives.' Q2 FY24 10-Q (Feb 27, 2024): adds 'Chief Executive Officer transition costs' and 'severance costs related to corporate restructuring.' Time elapsed 10-K -> 'comprehensive business review' = 65 days. Time elapsed 10-K -> CEO transition cost disclosure = 154 days.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The FY23 10-K's 'cost savings program + technology investment' strategy was effectively replaced within 65 days of filing by a 'comprehensive review' and CEO succession. Either (a) management knew of the impending review at 10-K signing and did not flag it as material to forward outlook (a disclosure-quality issue), or (b) the deterioration in late summer/fall 2023 was severe enough to force a strategic pivot in under a quarter (an operational-distress signal). Both readings are negative. This is the strongest Mode-B finding for CBRL: claim evolution velocity over four months reveals the 10-K's forward-looking sections were stale or aspirational at signing.

auditor_change.interpretation: 49-year auditor tenure, clean ICFR opinion, no resignation or disagreement language - high audit-quality posture; thesis is operational/capital-allocation, not accounting fraud.

going_concern.interpretation: No going-concern language anywhere in 10-K or pre-cutoff 10-Qs. Consistent with a still-profitable issuer with $25M cash + $543M revolver availability (after $156.5M drawn + $32.5M LCs of $700M facility) at Jan 26, 2024 - liquidity is finite but not acute.

insider_form4_pattern.interpretation: Insider posture is neutral - dominated by RSU/PSU grants and F-coded tax-withholding dispositions; only one small discretionary disposition (Word H L Jr, Mar 22, 2024). Not signaling acute distress (no panic selling) but also not opportunistic buying into the -47.5% drawdown. Modest counterweight against worst-case reading.

Chief Executive Officer transition costs (Q2 FY24 10-Q, 154 days after 10-K)

claim_evolution_10K_to_10Q.interpretation: Six material new operational/strategic disclosures within 5 months of the 10-K - high claim-evolution velocity for a non-acute-distress issuer. The 10-K's strategic posture and forward-looking outlook were effectively obsolete by the first post-filing 10-Q.

dividend_math.interpretation: Dividend coverage already inadequate in FY23 (115% payout) and dramatically worse H1 FY24 (183%). Dividend cut is mathematically implied without a sharp H2 FY24 recovery.

credit_structure.interpretation: $456.5M total debt vs $25.1M cash at FY23 close. 2026 refi cliff at materially higher rates (~6.5% straight-debt vs 0.625% current) implies ~$17.6M incremental annual interest = 15% of FY23 op income.

summary: CBRL's FY2023 10-K (filed 2023-09-26) presents a still-profitable casual-dining brand with a clean Deloitte audit (49-year tenure), no going-concern language, low supplier concentration, and full covenant compliance - none of the AAP-style accounting-fraud red flags. The thesis is instead operational and capital-allocation: (1) FY23 dividend payout ratio was already 115% of net income, and H1 FY24 (pre-cutoff) deteriorated to 183% as net income fell 33% YoY while the $1.30/qtr dividend was maintained; (2) the 10-K's 'cost savings program' strategy was effectively replaced within 65 days of filing by a 'strategic transformation initiative,' followed at 154 days by CEO transition costs and corporate-restructuring severance - high claim-evolution velocity revealing the 10-K's forward-looking sections were stale at signing; (3) comp guest traffic accelerated from -3.5% FY23 to -5.5% H1 FY24, with the brand's pricing-power lever (FY23 menu +8.6%) showing diminishing returns and softer follow-on increase (+4.8% Q2 FY24); (4) $300M 0.625% Convertible Notes mature June 2026, implying ~$17.6M of incremental annual interest if refinanced at current ~6.5% straight-debt rates; (5) Item 1A risk factors explicitly contemplate covenant-breach scenarios - unusual language for a steady cash-flowing restaurant and a sign management has modeled the downside. Auditor and insider postures are clean (no discretionary insider selling; only RSU mechanics and tax-withholding F-codes), which limits the worst-case framing - but Mode-B inference points to a probable dividend cut and structural earnings drag from the 2026 refi. Verdict: SHORT-tier on capital-allocation/operational grounds, with the caveat that this is NOT a lying-detector positive - disclosures are largely honest, just inadequately weighted in MD&A framing.
